_comment: Golden lookup files extracted from professional Cribl packs. Used as references for pipeline generation — when a sourcetype needs a lookup for normalization, these are the proven patterns.

parsing.description: Per-ASA-code regex patterns for field extraction (169 codes)
parsing.usage: Lookup by extracted ASA code → get regex for that specific message format

drops.description: ASA codes to drop (35 codes — no analytical value)

suppress.description: ASA codes to rate-limit via suppress (2 codes)

parsing.description: Per-FTD-code regex patterns for field extraction (168 codes)
parsing.usage: Same pattern as ASA — lookup by code, apply regex. FTD is structurally identical to ASA.

protocol.description: IP protocol number → transport name (100 protocols)

cim_action.description: FortiGate action → Splunk CIM action (28 mappings)

cim_severity.description: FortiGate level → CIM severity + severity_id (14 levels)
cim_severity.usage: Lookup level/crlevel/apprisk → CIM severity string + numeric id

sentinel_severity.description: FortiGate level → Sentinel LogSeverity + LogSeverityLabel (14 levels)

event_action_info.description: FortiGate event subtype action normalization (19 entries)

events_drop.description: FortiGate event type/subtype/eventtype → drop decision (92 entries)
events_drop.usage: Lookup by type+subtype+eventtype → if drop=1 then discard event

cef_to_commonsecuritylog.description: CEF extension key → CommonSecurityLog field name (137 mappings)
cef_to_commonsecuritylog.usage: Rename CEF short names to Microsoft Sentinel CommonSecurityLog schema names

fortinet_cef_mappings.description: FortiGate native field → CEF extension name (34 mappings)

cisco_asa_to_commonsecuritylog.description: Cisco ASA syslog field → CEF/CommonSecurityLog field (32 mappings)

ip_protocols.description: IP protocol number → protocol name (137 protocols, IANA standard)
ip_protocols.usage: Universal protocol normalization — works for any network log source

windows_event_codes.description: Windows Security Event IDs with keep/drop decision (776 codes)
windows_event_codes.usage: Lookup eventCode → keep=1 means security-relevant, keep=0 means droppable

firewall_ip_allowlist.description: Destination IPs whose traffic is routine (patch management, monitoring). Ships EMPTY — header only.
firewall_ip_allowlist.usage: Customer-populated allow-list, named directly by a lookup-driven OCSF optimization rule (never selected by sourcetype). An empty list makes the rule inert, which is the safe default for a drop.
firewall_ip_allowlist.source: customer-populated — no vendor knowledge is shipped

dns_top_domains.description: 100 globally well-known domains whose DNS queries are repetitive (search, social, cloud/CDN, dev, media, finance, e-commerce).
dns_top_domains.usage: Named directly by the DNS suppress-repeated-popular-domain-queries optimization rule to key its per-domain suppression window.
dns_top_domains.source: Hand-curated by Cribl SE, 2026-09-24 — editorially selected list of widely-recognized global domains, not derived from any third-party ranked list (e.g. Tranco); no ranking methodology or snapshot id applies.
dns_top_domains.license: n/a (no third-party data — domain names are public facts, not a licensed dataset)
